d: Jake gets married to a girl he just met. John buys a faux designer clock as a gift, which gets broken.
John helps a homeless man he discovered is a con artist when he learns the man is ill.
John panics when he has to get an MRI, finally resorting to Valium to get through the claustrophobic test.
John takes Reggies advice to be more sensitive with women. It helps at the office with Margaret, but backfires with a woman he is dating.
John is surprised when a patient is disappointed at the news that he's not terminally ill. Jake scams Bob in a Scrabble game.
Reggie goes out to dinner with her abusive friend Sara and Sara's husband, Richard. She finds that she and Richard are attracted to each other.
John tries to keep a casual love affair alive, while Bob tries to turn a found Super Bowl ring into his ticket to fame and fortune.
John believes that Christmas is a phony time of the year. Instead of embracing the Christmas spirit, he uses getting robbed as vindication for his position.
Reggie meets Johns's friend Dan, who is recently divorced from an extraordinary, accomplished woman.
Becker and the crew decide to barter services office visits for food and services.
Becker obsesses over whether or not younger women still find him attractive. Linda takes advantage of a hard-working temp.
Becker gets in hot water with parents when his nutrition lecture at an elementary school turns into a sex talk.
John gets a portable talking computer for his speech-impaired patient, with unintended consequences.
Becker bores a bartender with a story about his ex-wife's wedding.
Reggie decides to help Jake fulfill some of the dreams he had as a child, with disastrous consequences.
Dr. John Becker's laundry, apartment, and mail have all been tampered with and he is sure the culprit is one of his pesky neighbors.

Bob uses a questionable friend to get Reggie a great deal on a new freezer. John acts as a sex therapist for the Bennetts, an 80-year-old couple having difficulties because of Mr. Bennett's newly revived libido.
An unflattering picture of someone other than John is placed in an article about him, causing him distress.
When John receives some expensive steaks from a patient, his new neighbor Chris cajoles him into throwing a party.
John is surprisingly concerned when he learns that his new neighbor Chris has left town without saying goodbye.
Reggie and Chris compete for John's affection. Linda takes Margaret out for a night on the town.

st: Someone's In The Kitchen With Reggie?
d: John enters the diner from Reggie's apartment, trying to sneak out.
Now that Reggie is gone, John tells Chris he has feelings for her (Chris).
John sits on his fire escape, smoking a cigar, the smoke from which is wafting into Chris's open window directly above.
As John and Jake chat about Chris at the diner, Bob rushes in and announces that he just saw Chris naked when he went to fix her faucet.
Becker has a videotape of a French film that he plans to use to lure Chris into coming over to his place.
Becker tries to discourage a friend from expressing interest in Chris by telling him that she is gay.
At the diner, Chris is in the kitchen when a robber enters.
At the office, Margaret reveals to Linda that it's her ten-year anniversary of working for Dr. Becker.
At the diner, John expresses his repulsion for all the Christmas decorations.
Becker is upset when a patient substitutes his Christian Science faith for medical treatment.

One of John's patients, a high school student named Brad, comes in for a physical and John learns that the guy's sexually active, but isn't practicing safe sex. John performs an HIV test on Brad and tries to convince him to begin practicing safe sex.
John's at the end of his rope with his hectic practice and makes a call, which Linda overhears, telling the person on the other end that he can't take another day.
John helps his elderly neighbor, Mrs. Firth, get into her apartment and she repays him by making homemade chicken noodle soup.

st: I’ve Got Friends I Haven’t Used Yet
d: Bob is distraught because a thirty-something guy at his gym died while on the treadmill, and he's certain that he's headed for the same fate.
When a customer leaves the diner because of John's cigarette smoke, Chris puts her foot down and tells him that it is now a "smoke-free" restaurant.
John arrives at the diner and announces that he has quit smoking.
